Logistic Regression - with SMOTE (Kaggle fraud data)

Nao Mimoto – Class Web Page

  • 1. Load data
  • 2. Data Separation
  • 3. Baseline: logistic regression directly on the imbalanced data
  • 4. Apply SMOTE to the TRAINING data only
  • 5. SMOTE: logistic regression fit on the balanced data
  • CODE ONLY

1. Load data

(top)

SMOTE + Logistic Regression on the Kaggle “Credit Card Fraud Detection” dataset (anonymized European cardholder transactions, Sep 2013, ULB Machine Learning Group). 284,807 transactions, 492 frauds (0.173%) one of the most extreme real-world class imbalances in a public dataset. Kaggle page

rm(list=ls())   # clear the memory

library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(smotefamily)
library(pROC)
library(PRROC)

DF <- read_csv("creditcard.csv")
DF

#- Predict in Test Set
Test.prob = predict(Fit00, newdata=Test.set, type="response")

    ###----------
    ### a. Output ROC curve and AUC for all threshold
    library(pROC)
    auc.test = auc(factor(as.matrix(Test.resp)), Test.prob, levels=c("No", "Yes"))
    auc.test
## Area under the curve: 0.9726
    ###----------
    ### b. Output result for given threshold value
    threshold = .5   # pick a threshold

    #- Check the training set accuracy
    library(caret)
    Train.pred = ifelse(Train.prob > threshold, "Yes", "No")  # Turn the fitted values to Up/Down using threshold of .5
    Test.pred  = ifelse(Test.prob  > threshold, "Yes", "No")
    CM.train <- confusionMatrix(factor(Train.pred), factor(as.matrix(Train.resp)), positive="Yes")
    CM.test  <- confusionMatrix(factor(Test.pred),  factor(as.matrix(Test.resp)),  positive="Yes")

4. Apply SMOTE to the TRAINING data only

(top)

The function SMOTE() controls oversampling via dup_size (synthetic copies per real minority sample).

num_minority <- sum(Train.set$resp=="Yes")
target_minority <- nrow(Train.set)/10
dup_size <- round(target_minority / num_minority)
dup_size
## [1] 59
# Get names of columns except "resp".
feature_cols <- setdiff(names(DF00), "resp")
# Do the SMOTE
smote_out <- SMOTE(
  X = Train.set[, feature_cols],
  target = Train.set$resp,
  K = 5,
  dup_size = dup_size
)
Train.smote <- smote_out$data
names(Train.smote)[names(Train.smote) == "class"] <- "resp"
Train.smote$resp <- factor(Train.smote$resp, levels = levels(Train.set$resp))
Train.smote.resp = Train.smote$resp

cat("\nResampled Train.set class counts:\n")
## 
## Resampled Train.set class counts:
print(table(Train.smote$resp))
## 
##     No    Yes 
## 213242  21660
##----------
## Visualize SMOTE
DFo = Train.set %>% filter(resp=="Yes")
DFs = Train.smote %>% filter(resp=="Yes")

layout(matrix(1:2, 1, 2))
plot(DFo$V9, DFo$V8, col="red", pch=19)
plot(DFo$V9, DFo$V8, col="red", pch=19)
lines(DFs$V9, DFs$V8, type="p")

layout(matrix(1:2, 1, 2))
plot(DFo$V5, DFo$V4, col="red", pch=19)
plot(DFo$V5, DFo$V4, col="red", pch=19)
lines(DFs$V5, DFs$V4, type="p")

    Train.pred = ifelse(Train.prob > threshold, "Yes", "No")  # Turn the fitted values to Up/Down using threshold of .5
    Test.pred  = ifelse(Test.prob  > threshold, "Yes", "No")

    CM.test  <- confusionMatrix(factor(Test.pred),  factor(as.matrix(Test.resp)),  positive="Yes")

    CM.train            # Training set result

##----------------------------------------
## 4. Apply SMOTE to the TRAINING data only

num_minority <- sum(Train.set$resp=="Yes")
target_minority <- nrow(Train.set)/10
dup_size <- round(target_minority / num_minority)
dup_size

# Get names of columns except "resp".
feature_cols <- setdiff(names(DF00), "resp")
# Do the SMOTE
smote_out <- SMOTE(
  X = Train.set[, feature_cols],
  target = Train.set$resp,
  K = 5,
  dup_size = dup_size
)
Train.smote <- smote_out$data
names(Train.smote)[names(Train.smote) == "class"] <- "resp"
Train.smote$resp <- factor(Train.smote$resp, levels = levels(Train.set$resp))
Train.smote.resp = Train.smote$resp

cat("\nResampled Train.set class counts:\n")
print(table(Train.smote$resp))

DFs = Train.smote %>% filter(resp=="Yes")
